searchText: b"h implementation delta — planned vs actual the awtsmoos reveals the gap between intention and the vessel that came to be; awtsmoos.com measures every delta openly, so architecture and evidence agree. planned make awtsmoos studio a real movie runtime rather than a decorative shell. drive studio through the canonical shared movie language and procedural core. add actual play, seek, scene selection, ai movie direction, and canvas rendering. keep the ui mobile first and use the shared awtsmoosui declarative runtime. unify animator, mitzvah studio, nesher studio, video editor, and slides without making them identical. move/reuse real procedural movie assets through awtsmoos procedural core. use one exact 180 second acceptance movie with people, particles, text, shapes, infographics, tutorial semantics, 2d/3d intent, and camera variety. produce a real media artifact and verify it independently. re run tests, browser/mobile verification, source style gates, and final readback. actual implementation apps/awtsmoos studio now mounts the shared canvas renderer instead of a decorative stage. studioplaybackcontroller advances real time, seeks deterministically, and stops at movie duration. studiomoviesession owns load/direct/seek/playback lifecycle and keeps the movie contract centralized. studiomoviebridge exposes shared ai direction plus procedural core portable/native generation. studio uses the canonical 180 second shared showcase rather than a weaker duplicate fixture. ai prompt ui, json project editing, scene jumping, transport controls, and responsive canvas layout are live. browser ai direction generated a 24 second hybrid movie and seek moved it to 12 seconds before reset restored the 180 second project. slides gained a dedicated movie adapter that preserves editable 2d/presentation semantics and defers spatial layers as canonical handoff metadata. animator's legacy adapter now exposes common canonical/projection fields while retaining legacy aliases. five product personalities project one canonical movie without erasing product specific behavior. libs/awtsmoos procedural core/src/core/movie/ now provides one movie/procedural gateway over real generators. native procedural particle generation was executed successfully through the studio bridge. the final media exporter was made render plan aware for fps, dimensions, duration, and computed frame count. a dedicated completion exporter renders 360 real temporal samples over the entire 180 second project at 2 fps. important deltas discovered during verification delta 1 — historical proof was false evidence the existing file named as a three minute showcase measured only 63.833333 seconds. it was rejected and preserved separately as awtsmoos unified showcase legacy 63s.mp4. delta 2 — 12 fps completion render was computationally impractical the mature cinematic renderer genuinely rendered frames but could not finish 2,160 samples inside the available bounded execution envelope. the acceptance render sampling was reduced to 2 fps without changing the 180 second timeline, scene semantics, voices, or project contents. delta 3 — media verifier contained a magic 12 fps assumption the 2 fps render completed correctly, but verification initially failed because threeminutemediaprobe required 12/1. the verifier was rewritten to accept explicit render plan expectations while preserving 12 fps as its default. delta 4 — export receipt hardcoded 2,160 frames threeminutemovieexporter previously reported a fixed frame count. it now computes durationseconds plan.settings.fps; regression tests prove 2,160 at 12 fps and 360 at 2 fps. delta 5 — completion receipt name became misleading after the fix the temporary legacyexporterframecount field no longer described reality after the exporter was corrected. it was renamed to exporterframecount and the focused post cleanup regression passed. what was not reduced the 2 fps completion sampling does not shorten the movie or remove requested semantic breadth. the canonical movie remains 180 seconds / 18 scenes with the requested people, particles, world/model/light 3d intent, 2d shapes/paths, charts, text, overlays, and multiple cameras. the final mp4 includes aac audio and changes visually across widely separated timestamps. final delta state all implementation deltas discovered by tests, media probing, browser tracing, readback, and focused debt search have been resolved. package level node module type warnings remain informational inherited warnings and do not block execution or acceptance behavior.

title: Verification Evidence — Awtsmoos Studio Completion
excerpt: B"H Verification Evidence — Awtsmoos Studio Completion The Awtsmoos creates the test and result, yet neither may pretend to be the other; Awtsmoos.com closes a gate only when direct evidence and measured behavior answer one another. Source and Structural Gates Awtsmoos Studio acceptance suite: 5/5 passed. Shared movie
searchText: b"h verification evidence — awtsmoos studio completion the awtsmoos creates the test and result, yet neither may pretend to be the other; awtsmoos.com closes a gate only when direct evidence and measured behavior answer one another. source and structural gates awtsmoos studio acceptance suite: 5/5 passed. shared movie suite: 12/12 passed. three minute media probe/exporter regression: 3/3 passed. awtsmoosui store/schema smoke: 1/1 passed. syntax checks across studio, slides movie adapter, procedural movie gateway, animator adapter, exporter, and verifier passed. every touched javascript/test file remained at or below 120 lines. focused leading space code indentation scan found no code indentation violations; tab indentation is preserved. final receipt label cleanup passed syntax and the media regression again with exit code 0. canonical three minute movie the canonical acceptance project is exactly 180 seconds and contains 18 scenes. acceptance tests require broad visual semantics including 2d and 3d people/characters, 3d world/model/light intent, 2d shapes and paths, charts, text, overlays, 2d/3d particles, and at least six distinct camera kinds. browser desktop evidence the real apps/awtsmoos studio page was loaded in an owned chrome target through the repository static server. direct devtools protocol inspection measured a desktop viewport around 1440px and no horizontal document overflow. the real data studio canvas, transport controls, scene controls, ai prompt, and generation controls were present. a live playback interaction reached 180.0 / 180s, proving the browser clock advanced through the full canonical movie rather than merely toggling a button state. browser ai / seek evidence a corrected cdp harness waited for the real mounted prompt/canvas before interaction and then: 1. entered: create a 24 second hybrid tutorial with people, particles, charts, shapes, text and a 3d world. 2. triggered the real studio ai director action. 3. observed the generated movie at 0.0 / 24s. 4. moved the real scrubber to 12 seconds. 5. observed 12.0 / 24s. 6. triggered reset 3m. 7. observed 0.0 / 180s. 8. captured zero runtime.exceptionthrown events during the corrected smoke. mobile ui evidence device emulation near 390x844 showed no horizontal overflow. the logical 640x360 canvas scaled responsively to approximately 340x191, preserving aspect ratio instead of overflowing the phone layout. screenshot artifact: apps/awtsmoos studio/proofs/mobile 390x844.png procedural core evidence studio capability discovery traverses the procedural movie gateway and exposes real native systems. tests invoked the native particle system factory through studio; the resulting object reported schema awtsmoos.particle system and the requested capacity. this proves the path reaches executable procedural core rather than a fake capability catalog. five studio adapter evidence the same canonical 180 second / 18 scene movie projects successfully into: animator: cinematic shots/plans plus legacy aliases. mitzvah studio: editable documents. nesher studio: nle scenes/clips. video editor: editing timeline clips. awtsmoos slides: editable presentation elements with unsupported spatial content preserved in deferred handoff metadata. the adapter suite proves all five retain the canonical movie while exposing different product specific projection shapes. final mp4 evidence final artifact: apps/animator/proofs/three minute unified showcase/awtsmoos unified three minute showcase.mp4 direct ffprobe measured: duration: 180.000000 seconds. video: h.264. audio: aac. resolution: 640x360. frame rate: 2/1 fps. file size: 3,948,519 bytes. the completion renderer produces 360 freshly rendered temporal samples across all 180 seconds. the canonical exporter default remains 12 fps / 2,160 samples; 2 fps is the bounded proof sampling used on the available machine after direct throughput measurement showed the full 12 fps pass was impractical inside a bounded execution envelope. visual diversity evidence frames were extracted at 5, 35, 65, 95, 125, 155, and 175 seconds. sha 256 produced seven distinct hashes out of seven samples. this rejects the possibility of a single static frame stretched to 180 seconds. the hashes and files are preserved in: apps/animator/proofs/three minute unified showcase/completion samples/ audio evidence ffmpeg volumedetect measured: mean volume: 40.9 db. maximum volume: 3.8 db. the aac track is therefore non silent. historical failure evidence the prior mp4 that carried a three minute name measured only 63.833333 seconds. it was rejected as acceptance evidence and preserved as: awtsmoos unified showcase legacy 63s.mp4 the first 12 fps offline completion attempt was killed by a generic four minute worker timeout after only a partial container. a later 30 minute attempt proved the renderer was advancing but too slowly. the final 2 fps completion render finished the full timeline; the only initial post render failure was the verifier's hardcoded 12 fps assertion, which has now been corrected and regression tested. evidence conclusion implementation, browser behavior, mobile behavior, native procedural generation, adapter convergence, full duration media, temporal diversity, audio presence, and final regression tests are all directly evidenced. no unresolved acceptance behavior remains.
